pr_title: core: check dbus state before starting services with Type=dbus

issue_context.title: core: fix use of manager_dbus_is_running()
issue_context.body:
This is just a reminder.
53964fd26b4a01191609ffc064aa8ccccd28e377 (#27579) needs to be fixed.

review_comments:
Apparently in my PR I overlooked the fact that dbus can be manually stopped...was thinking it shouldn't be. But I think this change still suffers from the same problem, i.e. if dbus is inactive then we'll refuse the start?

Rethinking about this, what we want to avoid is just job type conflict here. So maybe `unit_stop_pending(manager_get_unit(m, SPECIAL_DBUS...))` is sufficient?

> But I think this change still suffers from the same problem, i.e. if dbus is inactive then we'll refuse the start?

I think UNIT_DEACTIVATING state should also be checked.

> I think UNIT_DEACTIVATING state should also be checked.

There's no need tho? When the stop job is already running, a new start job would just wait until that completes. As it doesn't cause job type conflict, it won't be canceled.
@Geass-LL Could you please test whether a running stop job also interrupts the reboot?

> @Geass-LL Could you please test whether a running stop job also interrupts the reboot?

If there is a running stop job, systemd will wait for this job until timeout, but this job won't interrupt the reboot.

> > I think UNIT_DEACTIVATING state should also be checked.
> 
> There's no need tho? When the stop job is already running, a new start job would just wait until that completes. As it doesn't cause job type conflict, it won't be canceled.

Guess you're right. If a service goes to UNIT_DEACTIVATING state but doesn't have a pending stop job, this means this service is not stopped by systemd, i.e. killed by SIGTERM sent from other process. Here, we only want to refuse the service activation request when dbus-broker is being stopped by systemd's job.
Hmm, this revert doesn't make a huge difference I think. We can't set up the handler for `ActivationRequest` if dbus isn't running after all 🤔

Not sure, but to support the following case, `manager_unit_inactive_or_pending()` is better, I think.
1. AddMatch method call for ActivationRequest succeeds,
2. stopping dbus.service (or .socket) is requested, and stop job is queued,
3. ActivationRequest signal is received. (dbus.service may be still running.)
I think this is exactly what we're trying to avoid in the first place? `Type=dbus` units pull in `dbus.{service,socket}`, and that would cause job type conflict...
